Compañía General de Combustibles (CGC).why: Page states oil and gas company, owned by the Eurnekian family, control acquired by Corporación América, Sociedad Comercial del Plata with the remaining 30%, stakes in TGN, GasAndes and TGM, and 'a fines de 2019, CGC alcanzaba una producción récord de 37.000 boe/d'.

Cyprus Popular Bank (Laiki).why: Central Bank of Cyprus release: Greek branches sold to Piraeus Bank; Cyprus business sold to Bank of Cyprus 'excluding its subsidiaries and foreign branches'; deposits up to EUR 100,000 transferred with effect from 26 March 2013; deposits above that remain in the 'bad' Laiki Bank. Bank of England note confirms it was a Cypriot bank trading as Laiki Bank UK.

De Beers.why: Page: 'the world's leading diamond company, operating across diamond exploration, mining, sorting, trading, the development of consumer brands', synthetic diamonds for industrial use, Anglo American plc 85% and Government of Botswana 15%. (The same page also gives a London headquarters address, which the description does not claim.)

Dongfang Electric Corporation.why: Interim report: wind, solar, hydro, nuclear, gas and thermal power equipment, chemical containers, energy-saving/environmental equipment and hydrogen products, engineering contracting; state-owned legal person capital RMB1,772,966,194; 340,000,000 H shares (Hong Kong) alongside 3,050,360,326 A shares; operating revenue RMB38,151m for H1 2025; 18,511 employees at 30 June 2025.

EVN Group.why: Report: electricity, gas and heat, networks including internet and telecommunications, drinking water and wastewater, thermal waste utilisation; 'EVN's headquarters are located in Lower Austria'; Vienna Stock Exchange (ATX); revenue EUR 3,000.0m in 2024/25; 7,997 employees at 30 September 2025; active in 12 countries including Bulgaria and North Macedonia.

East African Crude Oil Pipeline (EACOP).why: Page: 1,447 km from Kabaale, Hoima district, Uganda to the Chongoleani Peninsula near Tanga Port, Tanzania; 'some $4 billion'; shareholder logos TotalEnergies, UNOC, TPDC, CNOOC with no percentages; offices in Kampala, London and Dar es Salaam.

Ecopetrol.why: 20-F: organised under the laws of Colombia with principal offices in Bogotá; 'We are the largest company in Colombia'; operates across the hydrocarbon chain; through ISA has electricity transmission and toll roads; the Nation owns 88.49% of voting capital; Colombian Stock Exchange from the August 2007 IPO and ADSs on the NYSE from September 2008; group production 736.6 mboed in 2023.

Enagás.why: Page: Technical Manager of the Spanish gas system; certified by the European Commission as an independent TSO since August 2012; over 12,000 km of pipelines, 8 LNG terminals, 3 underground storage sites across 8 countries; listed on the Ibex 35 since its 2002 debut with a 90% free float.

Energo-Pro.why: Page: founded 1994, registered address Prague 1; electricity generation, distribution, sales and trading with a hydropower focus; Jaromír Tesař founded it and became 100% owner in 2016; 54 hydropower plants in 5 countries; more than 2.6 million distribution customers in Bulgaria and Georgia.

Eni.why: Page: hydrocarbon exploration and production, renewables (Plenitude), biofuels and sustainable chemistry (Enilive), carbon capture; 1.73 million boe/d, 31,523 Eni people, 62 countries, data updated 31 December 2025; registered head office in Rome. Identical wording to the 'Eni S.p.A.' entry.

Eni S.p.A..why: Same page and same claims as the 'Eni' entry; wording is identical, as intended for one company.

Elektroprivreda Srbije (EPS) / RB Koluba.why: Consolidated statements: joint-stock company registered in that form by the Business Registers Agency on 13 April 2023; Republic of Serbia holds 100% of the shares; electricity production, supply and trading plus coal production, processing and transport; 19,725 employees at 31 December 2024; revenue from contracts with customers RSD 442,630,450 thousand in 2024; 'Rudarski basen Kolubara' a production unit with open-pit fields Polje C, Polje G and Polje E.

Compañía Minera Antamina.why: Sustainability report: polymetallic mine in Ancash (San Marcos, Huari), copper, molybdenum, zinc, silver, lead (and bismuth), Punta Lobitos port in Huarmey, 2,955 direct employees at end-2021, revenues US$5,328 million in 2021. Teck's page maps the shares: Glencore 33.75%, BHP 33.75%, Teck 22.5%, Mitsubishi 10%, and calls it an open-pit operation.

Delta & Pine Land.why: Release of 1 June 2007: 'Delta and Pine Land Company is a commercial breeder, producer and marketer of cotton planting seed', also breeds, produces and markets soybean planting seed; Monsanto 'has completed its acquisition of D&PL for approximately $1.5 billion in cash'. The entry describes the named company, not the parent.

Doğu Biga Madencilik.why: Article: Alamos Gold's Turkish subsidiary holding the Kirazlı, Ağı Dağı and Çamyurt projects in north-western Türkiye; sale to Tümad Madencilik for total cash consideration of $470 million, expected to close in Q4 2025.

DynCorp.why: Company history: private and employee-owned ('one of the largest employee-owned firms in the United States'), Reston, Virginia address and 1999 Reston headquarters, Defense Department logistics support (just under half of revenue), state and local government services, information technology, sales of $1.81 billion in 2000.

Edison.why: Page: 'Italy's second-largest energy company'; Edipower described as 'Edison's wholly-owned subsidiary'; EDF 'now holds in excess of 80% of the shares of Edison' (2012); acquisition of Delmi's shareholding for EUR 784 million; overall deal value approximately EUR 3.8 billion.

Ecuacorriente S.A. (CRCC-Tongguan).why: Article: 'Mirador is run by Ecuacorriente, a subsidiary of the Chinese consortium CRCC-Tongguan'; open-pit copper mine in Zamora Chinchipe; 30-year concession; production began July 2019; total investment of more than $2 billion over the concession period.

Ecuagoldmining South America S.A..why: Article: holder of the Río Blanco concession in Molleturo parish, Cuenca; work began August 2016; suspended since May 2018; shareholders Junefield Gold Investments Limited and Power Fortune Development Limited, both based in Hong Kong; Junefield formally began arbitration against Ecuador in October 2022.

Electron Investment S.A. (EISA).why: Annual report: sociedad anónima under Panamanian law by Public Deed No. 297 of 10 January 1984; development and administration of generation plants and purchase and sale of energy; Monte Lirio 51.6 MW operating since 1 October 2014 and Pando 34 MW since 18 October 2019 on the Río Chiriquí Viejo, Chiriquí, 86 MW combined; shareholders at 31 December 2024 Genera Avante S.L. (Inveravante) 58.53%, Aurel S.A. (Grupo Eleta) 31.52%, COFIDES with FIEX 9.95%.

ESP and ESSA2 SpA into Enel Colombia S.A. ESP. The release gives no day-of-month for the approval itself, so 'March 2022' is as precise as the source allows.

Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation o.why: Press brief: registered 30 October 2006 under the Companies Act 1956; Special Purpose Vehicle under the administrative control of the Ministry of Railways, which holds 100% of its equity; planning, development, financing, construction, maintenance and operation of the Dedicated Freight Corridors; EDFC 1,840 route km, WDFC 1,502 route km.

Descon Engineering.why: Profile: legal residence Pakistan; integrated engineering services and manufacturing for energy, infrastructure and process industries, engineering through to maintenance; operates in Pakistan and the Middle East; 'more than 25,000 workers, about 50% of them overseas', with no year given, exactly as the description says.

EDF Renewables.why: 2018 release: EDF Energies Nouvelles renamed (EDF Renewables adopted by international subsidiaries in April 2018, EDF Renouvelables in France September 2018); wind and solar development, construction and operation and maintenance for own account and for third parties; 14.2 GW gross installed capacity. 2025 release dated 17 June 2025: merger with the EDF Group International Division to form EDF power solutions, 31 GW installed, 10,000 employees, 25 countries.

Drummond Ltd..why: Drummond Ltd.'s own figures sheet: La Loma, El Descanso and El Corozo in Cesar and Magdalena; Puerto Drummond loading capacity 60 million metric tons a year; 25.1 million metric tons exported in 2025; 5,160 direct employees and 5,533 contractors at 31 December 2025; 'In 1995, coal production began.' The sheet gives no headquarters and never mentions the US parent, and the description claims neither.

Electricity Development Corporation (EDC.why: Presidential decree signed 29 November 2006: 'une société à capital public dénommée ELECTRICITY DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION'; Article 2 covers managing public assets in the electricity sector for the State, studying/preparing/carrying out electricity infrastructure projects entrusted by the State, promoting investment, and taking shareholdings in electricity companies.

Engen Petroleum.why: Engen profile: 'an Africa-based energy company' in the downstream refined petroleum market, refining, marketing and convenience retail; Durban refinery nameplate 135,000 b/d; presence in over 20 countries; approximately 1,500 service stations across sub-Saharan Africa and the Indian Ocean Islands. Digital Refining, dated 23 May 2024: Petronas sold its 74% shareholding to Vivo Energy, completing that day, with Phembani Group remaining a 21% shareholder in the South African business.

Dow Chemical.why: The report says Dow Inc. was incorporated in 2018 as a holding company and operates all its businesses through TDCC, a wholly owned subsidiary, but it does not date the start of that subsidiary relationship. Cut 'since 2018'. Everything else checks out: incorporated in Delaware in 1947 as successor to an 1897 Michigan corporation; polyethylene and other ethylene derivatives, polyurethanes, construction chemicals, coating materials and silicones; Dow Inc. net sales $39,968m and about 34,600 full-time employees at 31 December 2025; NYSE symbol DOW.

Daewoo Engineering and Construction.why: The cited company page (summary.asp) now returns an error page: only its metadata ('1973년 설립, 종합건설회사') and navigation could be read, so it cannot carry the facts on its own. A second page on the company's own site (business.asp) opened and states the 1973 founding, the general-construction description, the five business areas (civil engineering, plant, building, housing, development) and a Seoul address; added as a source. KHL confirms Jungheung Group's purchase of a 50.75% stake held by Korea Development Bank, reported complete in an article dated 13 December 2021, for 2.1 trillion won (US$1.8 billion). Description left as written.

Dundee Precious Metals.why: The company page carries the 'Canadian based, international gold mining company engaged in the acquisition, exploration, development, mining and processing of precious metals' wording, the four operating countries (Bulgaria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Ecuador) and 'TSX: DPM'. The 12 September 2025 release confirms the name change to DPM Metals Inc. but does not mention Adriatic Metals, so the 'after buying Adriatic Metals' clause was unsupported; the 3 September 2025 release, which states the Adriatic acquisition completed on 3 September 2025 and the name change taking effect 12 September 2025, was opened and added as a source. Description left as written.

Eiffage.why: The page never calls Eiffage French: it says 'Eiffage is one of the leading European construction and concessions companies' and that the group is 'deeply rooted in France'. Elecnor.why: The results release does not call the group Spanish and does not mention substations, solar parks or railway electrification: it describes 'essential services' for electricity, telecoms, water, transport and energy distribution, and sustainable projects in renewables and transmission lines mainly in Australia, Brazil and Chile. The group's own site, which opened, calls it 'uno de los más destacados grupos empresariales españoles' and Elecnor 'una compañía global de infraestructuras, energía y servicios' with activity areas including electricity, power generation, telecommunications, railways, construction, water and the environment; added as a source and the description rewritten to those terms. The 51% of Celeo with transmission lines in Chile, Brazil and Peru and group sales of 3,810.1 million euros in 2024 are in the release and stand.

It also does not place Capa Circa near Amayapampa (only that the mineralization is similar). Cut the invented line of business for Da Capo, used the filing's own wording for Vista Gold, and dropped 'nearby'.

Daewoo Motor Co..why: The article confirms the Incheon Court's approval of the reorganisation plan on 30 September 2002, the 17 October 2002 transfer of three manufacturing plants (Changwon, Kunsan and the Hanoi operations) and nine overseas subsidiaries to GM Daewoo Auto & Technology, the Bupyung plant becoming Daewoo Inchon Motor Company, and that facilities, subsidiaries, debts and liabilities outside the agreements stayed with creditors. Doe Run Peru.why: The 10-K confirms the 23 October 1997 purchase of the La Oroya complex from a Centromin subsidiary, the August 1998 Cobriza purchase, Doe Run Cayman Ltd.'s holding of more than 99% with present and former employees holding the rest as Peruvian law requires, Renco Group's indirect ownership, and the 31 October 2003 counts of 841 salaried and 2,296 hourly employees plus 957 contractors. The $435.5 million figure is La Oroya's net sales for fiscal 2003 excluding sales to Doe Run, not the company's total, so it has been attributed that way.

Endesa / Enel.why: Endesa's page verifies 'the leading company in the Spanish electricity sector', producing, distributing and selling electricity and gas, about 10,000 employees and more than 10 million customers, Enel Group ownership of 70.10% and joining the group in the first quarter of 2009.
